video_title: Is Doc Rivers Right About Giannis???

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Iman Shumpert and Arhii Shumpert discuss Giannis Antetokounmpo's role as a point guard
quotes.excerpt: It's a tweener position. It throws the team off. It's unsettling. Somebody has to make that work.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: It's a tweener position. It throws the team off. It's unsettling. Somebody has to make that work.

text_blocks.speaker: Arhii Shumpert
text_blocks.text: It's a tweener position, but at the same time, it's not when you're looking at him and you're out there on the floor. Looking at Giannis play, I wouldn't think he's in between the three and the four. I would think he's a four who can just do things a three can do.

quotes.social_post: Iman Shumpert on Giannis Antetokounmpo playing point guard: It is a tweener position that throws the team off. He is a four who can do things a three can do, but it is unsettling for the team.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: The challenge of playing Giannis Antetokounmpo at the wing position
quotes.excerpt: It's hard to place Giannis on a team and have him play the wing.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: People don't realize that's the challenge with Giannis. It's hard to place Giannis on a team and have him play the wing because he ruins the spacing.

text_blocks.speaker: Arhii Shumpert
text_blocks.text: He ruins the spacing. So it's smarter to have him attack downhill from the top.

quotes.social_post: Iman Shumpert argues that playing Giannis Antetokounmpo at the wing ruins the spacing. He believes it is much smarter to have him attack downhill from the top.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo needs complementary players like Khris Middleton and Jrue Holiday
quotes.excerpt: He needs to have other players who don't need a lot in order for them to get their game going.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: He needs to have other players who don't need a lot in order for them to get their game going.

text_blocks.speaker: Arhii Shumpert
text_blocks.text: Exactly. Chris Middleton. Exactly. You miss a player like Chris Middleton. You miss players like that because it's almost like all you have to do is add water.

quotes.social_post: Iman Shumpert on the Bucks needing players like Khris Middleton: You miss players like that because it is almost like all you have to do is add water.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo is not a natural point guard
quotes.excerpt: Giannis is not a natural point guard.
quotes.quote: Giannis is not a natural point guard. When he's talking about super IQ, most people that are heads-y, capable players, they're just crafty and understanding of each moment. That's what a point guard is for. The point guard is for that because usually, your point guard, though he can do stuff, he's not the highest-jumping, scoring sensation. He just understands the game. It's like somebody that can keep the checks and balances for you. The problem is when having the point guard there, Giannis needs to attack from there, otherwise you can build a wall for Giannis.
quotes.social_post: Iman Shumpert says Giannis Antetokounmpo is not a natural point guard. He argues that Giannis needs to attack from the point, otherwise teams can easily build a wall against him.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo needs to adopt a more traditional power forward role
quotes.excerpt: He's going to have to start picking and popping. He's got to become Zach Randolph.
quotes.quote: He's going to have to start picking and popping. He's got to become Zach Randolph. You're going to be the more vicious version of Zach Randolph, but it's got to become catching the ball at the pinch post and letting somebody fly off for a handoff. Letting guards be guards and letting them set you up a little bit as opposed to you having to do so much thinking.
quotes.social_post: Iman Shumpert says Giannis Antetokounmpo needs to evolve his game: He has to become a more vicious version of Zach Randolph, catching the ball at the pinch post and letting guards set him up instead of doing so much thinking.
